extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads() enables remote code execution — Full remote code execution on the server; attacker can execute arbitrary Python code, access the database, read/write files, and compromise all patient PHI/PII. [verified: Same as idx 0/14: request.body/GET.blob → pickle.loads() at line 70; _wrk_gate gates but does not sanitize — token knowledge yields full RCE.]

Code injection via eval() with user-controlled expression — Potential remote code execution through Python eval sandbox escape; attacker can execute arbitrary Python commands on the server. [verified: Same as idx 1/16: GET 'expr' → eval() at line 88; __builtins__ restriction bypassable via type introspection for arbitrary code execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 user-controlled fragment — Remote code execution via SSTI; attacker can execute arbitrary Python, read sensitive files including database credentials and SECRET_KEY, and pivot to the database. [verified: Same as idx 2/15: GET 'fragment' → Jinja2 Template concatenation at line 137; no sanitization enables SSTI-to-RCE.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template with User Input — Remote code execution, arbitrary file read, disclosure of SECRET_KEY and all environment variables, full server compromise. [verified: Same as idx 2: GET 'fragment' concatenated into Jinja2 Template.render() at line 137 with no sanitization — classic SSTI to RCE.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY — Forgery of session cookies and CSRF tokens, enabling complete account takeover and bypass of all CSRF protections. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback at line 7-10; identical to finding 0. The value is publically known in source control, and if the env var is missing, session/CSRF token forgery becomes trivially possible.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY enables session forgery — Complete session and CSRF token forgery; attacker can impersonate any user including clinic admins and clinicians, accessing all patient PHI/PII. [verified: Same hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY at line 7-10; duplicate of findings 0 and 3. The committed fallback value enables session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is not set.]

Unrestricted File Upload Without Content Validation in Ops Endpoint — Arbitrary file write on the server, potential remote code execution via uploaded scripts, storage exhaustion. [verified: Same as idx 5: no extension whitelist, content-type validation, or path sanitization on FileSystemStorage.save() at lines 34/37; arbitrary file write possible.]

security finding — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, potentially enabling code execution [verified: FileSystemStorage.save() at lines 34/37 accepts user-controlled names (uploaded filename or GET 'packet_ref') with no path sanitization; '../' sequences enable writes outside private_exports/incoming/.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized user-controlled MongoDB query filter — Unauthorized data access from MongoDB, potential authentication bypass, data exfiltration, or denial of service via expensive queries. [verified: Same as idx 4: request.body JSON passed unsanitized as MongoDB filter at line 154; $where/$regex operator injection.]

XML External Entity injection via lxml with external entity resolution enabled — Arbitrary local file read (SECRET_KEY, database credentials, patient data) and server-side request forgery to internal network services. [verified: Same as idx 3/17: lxml XMLParser with resolve_entities=True at line 163-165 on request.body; XXE file read and SSRF.]

security finding — NoSQL query manipulation enabling data exfiltration or bypass of query constraints [verified: request.body JSON is used directly as a MongoDB query filter at line 154 with no operator allowlist; $where, $regex, $ne injection can bypass query logic or execute server-side JavaScript.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via lxml Parser with Entity Resolution Enabled — Arbitrary file read (including /etc/passwd, environment files with secrets), SSRF to internal services, potential denial of service via billion laughs attack. [verified: Same as idx 3: lxml parser with resolve_entities=True at line 163-165 processes untrusted request.body, enabling XXE file read and SSRF.]

security finding — Leakage of SECRET_KEY, database credentials, and source code paths through verbose error pages [verified: DEBUG defaults to True at line 11 via os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG','1')=='1'; the .env.example also sets DJANGO_DEBUG=1. Verbose error pages with stack traces, local variables, and Django settings (including SECRET_KEY and DB credentials) are exposed to unauthenticated users on any triggered error.]

security finding — Session hijacking via network sniffing of cookies sent over unencrypted HTTP [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT all default to False (off) at lines 125-129 via env defaults of '0', and .env.example sets all three to 0. Session and CSRF cookies are transmitted over plain HTTP without the Secure flag, enabling MITM session hijacking.]

Session and CSRF cookies missing Secure flag by default — Session hijacking via network sniffing on unencrypted connections; attacker can steal session cookies to impersonate any user including clinicians with access to PHI. [verified: Same missing Secure cookie flags at lines 125-126; duplicate of findings 2 and 5. SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE both default to False with no runtime override, and .env.example confirms the insecure defaults.]

Missing rate limiting on Django built-in login endpoint enables credential brute-force — Attackers can perform unlimited credential guessing against the /accounts/login/ endpoint to compromise user accounts including staff with access to PHI/PII. [verified: clinic_portal/urls.py:23 exposes Django's built-in /accounts/login/ via include('django.contrib.auth.urls'); requirements.txt contains no rate-limiting library (only Django+psycopg) and MIDDLEWARE in settings.py:30-36 has no throttling middleware — no lockout, delay, or attempt-limiting exists on the login endpoint.]

security finding — Unauthenticated access to uploaded PHI documents (PDFs, insurance cards, lab results) via /media/ URLs [verified: clinic_portal/urls.py:27-28 conditionally adds static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT) when DEBUG=True; DEBUG defaults to True (settings.py:15) and Django's static() view applies no authentication, leaving uploaded PHI documents at predictable /media/ paths accessible without login.]

Patient medical documents publicly accessible via MEDIA_ROOT in DEBUG mode — Unauthenticated access to uploaded patient medical documents including lab results, insurance cards, and clinical forms containing PHI/PII. [verified: Identical underlying issue to findings 0 and 2: the static() helper at clinic_portal/urls.py:27-28 serves MEDIA_ROOT directly without authentication when DEBUG=True, exposing all uploaded patient documents regardless of the auth checks on the document_download view.]

Hardcoded demo credentials grant administrative access to all demo users — Full administrative access to the clinic portal if demo data is present; attacker can access all patient records, prescriptions, appointments, and messages as clinic_admin (superuser). [verified: DEMO_PASSWORD='DemoPass123!' is hardcoded at seed_demo.py:35 and used for all demo users including a superuser (clinic_admin, is_staff=True, is_superuser=True); the password is publicly documented in README.md:49 with no environment guard preventing seeding in non-dev contexts, and once demo accounts exist in the database, anyone can authenticate via /login/ to gain full administrative access to a]

Missing Rate Limiting on Registration and Login Endpoints — Automated account creation (spam/DoS), password brute-force attacks leading to account compromise. [verified: The register view at /register/ has no rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or lockout; the login endpoint (Django built-in at /accounts/) similarly lacks any brute-force protection. Both are reachable unauthenticated and have no compensating controls.]

Missing authentication on internal ops endpoint exposing patient operational metadata — Unauthenticated access to operational metadata about patient records; information disclosure of clinic operational status and patient account metadata. [verified: Same as idx 7: patient_care_file_072 at line 50 has no _wrk_gate; unauthenticated disclosure of clinic operational metadata.]

Open redirect via user-controlled redirect target — Phishing and credential theft by redirecting authenticated users to attacker-controlled domains that mimic the clinic portal. [verified: Same as idx 8/18: GET/POST 'lane' → redirect() at line 58 without allowlist validation; open redirect to external URLs.]

Missing authentication on internal ops identity endpoint — Unauthenticated access to internal operations endpoint; enables reconnaissance of internal ops URL structure and could be used in combination with other attacks. [verified: Same as idx 13/23: patient_identity_ping_342 at line 99 lacks _wrk_gate; unauthenticated access to internal ops endpoint.]

CORS misconfiguration: origin reflection with credentials enabled — Cross-origin data theft; malicious websites can read API responses authenticated with the victim's session cookies, potentially exfiltrating patient data. [verified: Same as idx 6/19: Origin header reflected into ACAO with credentials=true at lines 119-121; credentialed cross-origin data theft.]

Cryptographically weak PRNG used for token/nonce generation — Predictable tokens enable token forgery or brute-force attacks against any system relying on these generated values for authentication or authorization. [verified: Same as idx 12/21: random.choice() at line 145 instead of secrets module; predictable token generation.]

Use of Insecure Pseudo-Random Number Generator for Token Generation — Predictable tokens enabling unauthorized access, bypass of token-based security controls. [verified: Same as idx 12: random.choice() at line 145 for token generation is non-cryptographic; outputs are predictable.]

security finding — API keys logged in server access logs and browser history, enabling key theft [verified: api_key_from_request() in portal/access.py reads the API key from request.GET.get('api_key'), a GET query parameter. The /api/availability/ endpoint (portal/urls.py:59) calls can_use_availability_api() which invokes this function, making API keys loggable in server access logs, proxy logs, browser history, and Referer headers with no compensating log-scrubbing middleware.]

API key accepted via GET query parameter exposing credentials in logs — API key leakage through server access logs, proxy logs, and browser history; attacker with log access can use captured keys to access the availability API and potentially other authenticated endpoints. [verified: Same root cause as findings 0 and 1: request.GET.get('api_key') in api_key_from_request() at portal/access.py line 222 exposes credentials in URL query strings. The availability API endpoint at /api/availability/ (portal/views.py:1202) gates access via can_use_availability_api(), which uses this function, making API keys leakable through standard web server access logging with no compensating cont]

security finding — Attackers can enumerate valid user accounts via registration error messages [verified: The register view (views.py:99) serves the form to unauthenticated users with no rate limiting; clean_email at forms.py:72-73 returns a distinct 'An account already exists for this email address.' error, allowing an attacker to enumerate which emails have patient accounts at this clinic—a PHI disclosure.]

User enumeration via distinct error message on duplicate email registration — Attacker can enumerate clinic patients by email address, confirming which individuals receive care at this facility and enabling targeted phishing or social engineering attacks. [verified: Identical reachable user-enumeration sink at forms.py:75; the distinct ValidationError message confirms account existence to anonymous attackers with no compensating control, constituting a PHI leak under HIPAA.]

security finding — Browser security mechanisms (XSS filter, CSP) disabled, increasing XSS attack surface [verified: X-XSS-Protection: 0 and Content-Security-Policy: '' are explicitly set at lines 127-128, disabling browser-enforced XSS protection for responses from this endpoint.]

SSL/TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound HTTPS requests — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections; attacker can intercept, read, and modify data sent to external services. [verified: Same as idx 11/22: ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 188; no certificate validation on outbound HTTPS.]

security finding — Disclosure of Django settings module path, aiding reconnaissance [verified: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment value is exposed in the JSON response at line 179, disclosing deployment configuration that aids reconnaissance.]

Environment Variable and Internal Path Disclosure via Ops Endpoint — Disclosure of deployment configuration and internal filesystem paths, facilitating targeted attacks against the application infrastructure. [verified: Same as idx 10: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR exposed at line 179; deployment reconnaissance aid.]

security finding — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections, enabling traffic interception [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 188 disables certificate validation for outbound HTTPS; target is hardcoded but the pattern eliminates MITM protection.]

SSL Certificate Verification Disabled for Outbound HTTPS Requests — Man-in-the-middle attacks intercepting or modifying data sent to external services, credential theft, data tampering. [verified: Same as idx 11: ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 188 disables certificate validation; MITM protection eliminated.]

CSV Formula Injection in Appointment and Visit Summary Exports — Arbitrary command execution on the machine of any staff member who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application, or credential harvesting via malicious hyperlinks. [verified: Appointment reason (line 1114) and summary diagnosis/care_instructions (line 1138) are written to CSV via csv.writer with no sanitization of formula-injection characters. No CSV escaping exists in the codebase; same low practical impact as finding [0] due to spreadsheet warnings.]

security finding — Arbitrary command/script execution when exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet software [verified: User-supplied diagnosis, care_instructions, and clinician_notes flow from VisitSummaryForm → DB → csv.writer with no sanitization of formula triggers (=, +, -, @); no CSV escaping or prefixing exists anywhere in the codebase. Modern spreadsheet apps warn users, limiting practical impact.]
